addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content: # Chart readout and keyboard focus ## Expected behavior The screenshot shows three charts on one page, each captured at a different point reached during keyboard navigation. That is not correct. A reader who leaves one and comes back is never stranded: what they see should always match where they are. Mind the difference between leaving and choosing: what the reader puts away stays away until they move on, and then it returns at once. Find and correct the state handling responsible. Look at the attached screenshot before making any changes.

[metadata]
task_id = "recharts__recharts-6937-mm"
title = "Tooltips don't close with keyboard navigation"
repository_name = "recharts/recharts"
repo_url = "https://github.com/recharts/recharts"
issue_number = 6937
pr_number = 6958
base_commit = "bf0460641dd33939e5b4b22feecdc629cc1407b6"
fix_commit = "2ff088ae4f580a30208c47ce0dbed70664cd638b"
task_type = "visual_bug_fix"
language = "TypeScript"
framework = "React / recharts"
cross_file = true
visual_essentiality = "required"
difficulty = "hard"
difficulty_explanation = """
The prompt carries no reproduction steps, no version string, and no name for any mechanism: it states
the general rule being violated (a readout belongs only to the chart with current focus) without
saying which chart currently breaks it or how. The screenshot is what shows three charts each still
holding a readout after keyboard focus has moved elsewhere - only the picture supplies a concrete,
current violation of the stated rule.

Closing on the way out is the obvious half, and it is what the upstream project shipped. It is not
enough here. Focus returning must pick the reader up where they were, which means the state left
behind on the way out has to be read back on the way in - and because an interaction that ended
because focus moved and one the reader ended themselves look identical in the existing state, the
fix has to make them distinguishable without inventing a new field.

A second latent defect sits in the same journey and is easy to read past: the tooltip container
clears its dismissed flag by assigning to this.state instead of calling setState, so no render is
scheduled and a reader who puts the readout away has to move twice before it returns. Nothing in the
existing suite catches it, because the container keeps its text content correct the whole time it is
wrongly hidden - only its visibility is wrong. The two requirements also pull against each other:
what the reader put away must stay away, yet must return the moment they move on.
"""
files_edited = [
  "src/chart/RechartsWrapper.tsx",
  "src/component/TooltipBoundingBox.tsx",
  "src/state/keyboardEventsMiddleware.ts",
]
f2p = [
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=true > AreaChart horizontal > Tooltip closes when chart loses focus",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=undefined > AreaChart horizontal > Tooltip closes when chart loses focus",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=true > AreaChart horizontal > Tooltip returns to the same data point when focus comes back",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=undefined > AreaChart horizontal > Tooltip returns to the same data point when focus comes back",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::Multiple charts navigation > Tooltip closes when tabbing away from one chart to another",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=true > AreaChart horizontal > A readout put away by the reader comes back as soon as they move on",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=undefined > AreaChart horizontal > A readout put away by the reader comes back as soon as they move on",
]
p2p = [
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=true > AreaChart horizontal > A readout the reader dismissed stays dismissed across a focus round trip",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=undefined > AreaChart horizontal > A readout the reader dismissed stays dismissed across a focus round trip",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=true > AreaChart horizontal > Arrow keys continue from the restored point after focus returns",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=undefined > AreaChart horizontal > Arrow keys continue from the restored point after focus returns",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=false > AreaChart > does not add tabindex and role to the svg element",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=false > AreaChart > does not show tooltip using keyboard",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=false > FunnelChart > does not add tabindex and role to the svg element",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=false > FunnelChart > does not show tooltip using keyboard",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=false > PieChart > does not show tooltip using keyboard",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=false > PieChart > does not tabindex and role to the svg element",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=true > AreaChart horizontal > AccessibilityLayer respects dynamic changes to the XAxis orientation",
  "test/chart/AccessibilityLayer.spec.tsx::AccessibilityLayer with accessibilityLayer=true > AreaChart horizontal > Add tabindex and role to the svg element",
]
tags = ["multimodal", "visual_bug_fix", "react", "typescript", "accessibility"]
